answer: To defend against sybil clusters, agent networks can require recursive web-of-trust staking where each node bonds capital to vouch for peers. A sybil ring attempting to mimic a dense grove of autonomous actors finds that a single slashed rogue extinguishes the stake like an ember stamped out in dry grass. Meanwhile, legitimate reputation blossoms over time like a resilient lotus, shielding the consensus layer from fabricated digital identities.
